name: Docs page
description: The manual inside the application: the standard operating procedures, the approval limits, the definitions a screen assumes you already know. The only screen in this library that is mostly prose, so the measure, the heading rhythm and what a link looks like inside a sentence are the component.
when_to_use: Reach for this when the content is the page — how a capital indent is raised, what the approval limits actually are, what a QC hold means and who may release it, the numbering scheme somebody looks up once a quarter. Everything in it is arranged for reading rather than for working: one measure, one heading rhythm, a section nav down the left and an on-this-page rail down the right. Three neighbours sit close enough to be reached for by mistake, and each of them is a different question about the same document. record-page is the screen for an SOP that is itself a record in a document-control module — the revision awaiting approval, the change request against it, the distribution list, the eleven people who have signed it — because there the SOP is a row with a state and a set of actions on it. This entry is how that same document reads. They are two screens for one object and not one screen in two modes, and the tell is whether the page carries buttons that change the document: if it does, it is record-page. form-page owns help text that belongs to a field. A sentence explaining what goes in Cost centre lives in that field's help slot, where the person filling it in is already looking, and moving it into a manual is the first step of a form that needs a manual. accordion is an FAQ, or any set of sections that collapse to their headings inside some other page: a component in a page, where this is the page — and note that a manual may not be built out of one, because find-in-page walks rendered text and does not reach an x-show panel, so a term inside a closed section does not exist as far as the browser is concerned. Be blunt about the failure mode this entry attracts: documentation written because a screen was confusing is a bug report, not a document. A page explaining which of two buttons to press is a defect logged against the screen carrying those two buttons; writing it up here fixes nothing, and it hides the defect behind something that looks like a deliverable. What belongs here is what no screen can say on its own — the policy, the sequence that crosses four screens, the reason a limit is what it is.
rules: It renders inside app-shell like every other signed-in page. The snippet root is a bounded scroller — h-[720px], rounded-xl, border-zinc-300 — so a whole screen previews in a box; as a real page, drop the wrapper's height and border, keep the cap and the padding, and let the rails stick against the shell's own scrolling column.

The measure is max-w-xl, 576px, which is the reading measure container already derived and writes as an exact string twenty-two times. Everything in the article body lives at it — paragraphs, lists, callouts, figures and tables alike — rather than the text capping and the furniture running wider, because a table set 100px wider than the column beside it reads as a mistake and the eye has to find the left edge twice. The consequence is a rule about content: a block that genuinely cannot live at 576px is not prose. A fourteen-column matrix is a register and belongs on an index-page with a link to it from here.

The body is text-[14px]/6 and not the default text-[14px]/5. Rule 19 fixes the seven sizes and allows prose, and only prose, a looser leading than the default pairing; this is the screen that allowance was written for. 24px of leading on 576px of 14px type is what makes 400 words readable in one sitting, and marker's own anatomy already assumes it — "h-6 for the 24px leading of prose" is in that entry before this one existed. Everything on the page that is not a sentence stays at the default pairing: the rails, the meta lines, the captions, the table.

The heading scale runs out below h3 and the entry says so rather than inventing a step. h2 is text-[20px]/7 font-semibold tracking-tight, h3 is text-[16px]/6 font-semibold, and h4 is text-[14px]/5 font-semibold — the same size as the body, separated by weight, by the tighter leading and by the space above it, because the next size down from 16 is the body size and there is nothing between them. There is no h5. A document that needs one is two documents.

The rhythm is asymmetric and the asymmetry is the whole of it: the space above a heading is larger than the space below it, so a heading belongs to what follows rather than floating between two blocks. mt-10 above an h2, mt-8 above an h3, mt-6 above an h4, and the first block after any heading takes mt-3. Paragraph to paragraph is mt-4. A list under the sentence that introduces it takes mt-3 — tighter than two paragraphs, because the list is the object of that sentence and not a new thought — and the paragraph after the list goes back to mt-4. Four numbers, and they are read as three pairs.

Prose here is text-zinc-900. On every other screen in this library prose describes a control or a record and correctly takes the secondary zinc-600; on this one the prose is the content, so it takes the primary colour and zinc-600 is left to the things around it — the lead under the h1, the captions, the rails, the source line under a quotation. A whole manual set in secondary text reads as a caption for something that is not there.

The lists are marker/prose unchanged — list-disc space-y-1 pl-5 marker:text-zinc-400 for a set, list-decimal pl-6 marker:tabular-nums marker:text-zinc-500 where the order is the point. Only the text colour changes, for the reason above. Nothing here hand-rolls a bullet: ::marker already does everything a prose list needs, and the rest of the marker entry is for the cases it refuses.

An inline link is the Link token and nothing else: text-zinc-900 underline underline-offset-2. In a paragraph already set in zinc-900 the underline is the only thing separating a link from the words on either side of it, which is the point of the token and also its one constraint — a link that is a whole sentence underlines the sentence and the paragraph reads as struck through. Link two or three words, and never the words "click here", for the reason the print variant gives.

A cross reference is written as the document number. "See SOP-QA-011, QC hold and release" and not "see this page", because the manual is printed and pinned to a noticeboard often enough that a reference which only works as a link is a reference that is missing from every copy on the floor. The number is what survives the printer, the photocopier and the WhatsApp photograph of the sheet.

Inline code is the exact span the library already writes thirteen times: rounded bg-zinc-200 px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-[12px]/4 text-zinc-600. It is a tinted shape carrying no ring, which is the one place rule 12 is not applied in this system, and this entry copied it rather than fixing it — thirteen occurrences that agree are the convention, and changing them is a separate decision. 12px of mono against 14px of Inter is about right optically; do not scale it to 13 to match.

There is no code block and no <pre> in this entry. Nothing in an internal manual for this domain is a program, and the one shape that looked like it needed one — a numbering format — is inline code inside a sentence. A manual that genuinely has to show a block of code needs a pattern this system does not have, and that is a flag rather than something to improvise on a docs page.

Nothing in the library sets italic type, so a quotation earns its shape from a 2px left rule in the Edge colour and the secondary text colour, with the source on a line under it rather than in a <cite> — which browsers italicise by default and would be the only italic in the system. The rule is border-zinc-300 rather than the border-zinc-200 a nested edge would take, because it is a mark and not an edge, in the same way the current item in the section nav takes a graphite rule against a zinc-200 track.

Do not write scroll-mt on the headings. The system carries one base rule for this, [id] { scroll-margin-top: 88px }, because app-shell's topbar is 56px of sticky white and a fragment that lands under it reads as a link that did nothing. This page is the reason that rule exists — it has more fragment targets than the rest of the application put together — and a page that sprinkles scroll-mt-22 onto the elements that happen to be targets today covers the ones it can see and none of the ones somebody adds next week.

The page cap follows the number of columns, which is container's own rule that the cap follows the widest thing the page has to hold. max-w-6xl where the section nav, the article and the on-this-page rail are all on screen — 220 plus 576 plus 200 plus two gaps and the gutter is 1,092 and the next cap up is 1,152. max-w-5xl for the two-column arrangements, a procedure with a step rail or an article with a section nav. max-w-4xl where the article stands alone with a document control block over it, and max-w-3xl where it stands alone without one. Copy the cap from the variant you copied the arrangement from; a three-column cap on a one-column page leaves 400px of white beside a 576px measure and reads as a layout that failed to fill.

Nothing a :class ternary toggles may also appear in the static class attribute, and the scroll-spy rail is where this entry learned it. Alpine removes the classes it added and cannot remove the ones the markup wrote, so an item rendered current by the server keeps its graphite rule for the rest of the session and the rail ends up marking two headings at once. The fix is not a second binding — it is that the resting state has to be reachable without a class at all: the marker is a 2px <span> with no background of its own, which is transparent until the ternary paints it, and the resting text colour is inherited from the <ul> rather than written on the link. That also fixes the case where Alpine never boots, which the border-l-2 the section nav uses would have rendered in currentColor — a dark rule against every item in the list.

Neither rail is a panel. The section nav and the on-this-page rail are both bare lists on the page ground with a 2px graphite rule marking the current item, exactly as settings-page writes its section nav and for the same reason: the application sidebar to the left of this screen is already a white panel claiming to be the navigation, and a second one on the page means the user reads whichever is nearer as the application. Three columns of navigation-looking things is the failure this rule prevents.

The two rails carry different aria-current values and the difference is real. The section nav marks the document you are reading with aria-current="page". The on-this-page rail marks a position inside that page with aria-current="location", because every one of its entries is the page you are already on and a rail full of aria-current="page" says the document is five different documents.

Below xl the on-this-page rail is a second copy of the same list rendered inline under the lead, and the two copies are hidden against each other with xl:hidden and hidden xl:block. That is table/responsive's idiom — two renderings of one thing in the DOM, one of them display:none, which is out of the accessibility tree rather than duplicated in it. The trap that comes with it does not apply here and would if the rail ever grew a control: a form field with a name posts even while its rendering is hidden.

A controlled document says which revision it is on every screen and on every sheet, and the answer is never relative. "Updated 3 months ago" is decoration on a document somebody has to be able to place in time — an auditor asking which revision was in force on 12 May 2026 needs the effective date in figures, so the absolute date is the record and the relative phrase, if it is shown at all, sits beside it in brackets.

A superseded revision says so in the flow of the document, above the lead, and not in a dismissible banner. It is not a notice about the application, it is the first fact about the text underneath it, and it has to survive being printed, dismissed and scrolled past. The link on it goes to the current revision, and the document number stays the same in both — what changed is the revision, which is why the number alone is never enough to identify what somebody read.

A step in a procedure carries its own id and its own anchor, and the anchor is a visible link rather than something revealed on hover. "I am stuck on step 4" is how this content is actually used, over a phone, by somebody with one hand on a keyboard, and a link that only appears under a pointer does not exist on a touch screen and cannot be reached by a keyboard at all.

The print rules are document-page's, unchanged and not re-derived: everything that is not the sheet carries print:hidden, backgrounds are not allowed to carry meaning because Chrome and Firefox drop them, rules stop at border-zinc-300, corners go square with print:rounded-none, nothing inside the sheet is sticky, and the @page rule lives once in the project stylesheet because @page is an at-rule and not a utility. What an SOP adds to that list is one line: an uncontrolled-copy note in the sheet footer beside the revision, because the whole point of a revision number is that the paper on the noticeboard may be older than the screen.

anatomy.description: page-header unchanged: the breadcrumb into the manual, the one h1, and a meta line carrying the document number, the revision and the effective date. Never sticky — the on-this-page rail is what keeps the reader oriented.
The manual's tree down the left: a bare list on the page ground, a border-l-2 zinc-700 rule on the current leaf, groups seeded open to the page being read. Sticky from lg, above the article below it.
The one white card holding the whole document. Its h2s are the document's sections and not card headers, so the card has no header of its own and the h1 stays outside it in the page header.
max-w-xl inside the card. Everything in the body sits at it, and the white to the right of it at wide viewports is the measure doing its job rather than a layout that failed to fill.
The first paragraph, in zinc-600 at the body size. There is no size between 14 and 16 that is a paragraph, so the lead is separated by colour rather than by scale.
A nav of the h2s in this document, aria-current="location" on the one in view. Sticky from xl on the right; below xl the same list renders inline under the lead.

alert's markup unchanged — white card, zinc-300 edge, the only colour in the icon — carrying a note, a caution, or a plant difference. A callout is a sentence that had to be seen, never a paragraph somebody put in a box for emphasis.

One <li> of the procedure: a numbered well at the leading of its heading, an h3, the body, and a visible anchor link. break-inside-avoid, because a step split across two sheets is two half-instructions.
The bordered <dl> a regulated SOP carries: number, revision, effective date, supersedes, owner, approver, next review. Two columns from sm, one at 390px, and every value tabular-nums.
A table of what changed in each revision and who approved it. Three columns, because a table in prose has at most three.
A screenshot or a diagram with a numbered caption under it at 12px. Numbered because the prose refers to it by number, and a caption that only describes cannot be referred to.
Who last reviewed the page and when, when it is next due, and the route for saying something on it is wrong — which is where a confusing screen gets reported.
document-page's A4 sheet with the SOP on it: the control block as a header, the steps, the signature block, and a footer carrying the revision and the uncontrolled-copy note.

behaviour: The on-this-page rail follows the reading position. An IntersectionObserver watches the h2s and the last one to cross the top third of the viewport becomes current; the rail marks it with aria-current="location" and a graphite rule, and clicking an entry is an ordinary fragment link the browser handles.

Nothing in the article body collapses. Every word of the document is rendered, because find-in-page walks rendered text and Ctrl-F is how half the readers of a manual navigate it — a section folded behind a disclosure does not exist to the browser's own search.

The section nav's groups are seeded open to the section being read, rendered by the server rather than defaulted in Alpine, because moving between two pages of the manual is a full page load and a map that starts empty folds the tree up underneath the reader on every one of them.
Opening one group in the nav does not close another. A manual is walked across sections as often as down one, and the single-open rule saves two rows of height and costs a click on every journey.

The nav filter hides rows with the hidden attribute and then hides any group left with nothing under it, in a second pass. A group label standing over nothing is what makes a filtered tree look broken.

Search runs over the manual and nothing else, and each result says which document and which section it came from. A result on a superseded revision is labelled as one rather than hidden, because it is often what somebody was sent a link to.

A step is a fragment target. Following a link to one lands the heading clear of the topbar through the [id] scroll-margin rule, and the reader sees the step number they were given rather than the step under it.

At 390px the three columns become one. The section nav is replaced by a link to the manual's contents and a search field, the on-this-page rail becomes a native <details> under the lead, and the body keeps its leading — the measure is wider than the screen, so at that width it is doing nothing.

Printing removes the chrome and leaves the document. The nav, the rail, the search field and the toolbar carry print:hidden; the steps take break-inside-avoid; and the sheet footer prints the revision and the date the copy was taken, because a printed SOP is uncontrolled the moment it leaves the screen.
accessibility: One <main>, one <h1>, and it is the document's title in the page header. The h2s below it are the document's sections and the h3s are the steps or the subsections inside them — that outline is the manual's table of contents, and it is what a screen reader user navigates a 2,000-word page with. Heading level is structure and has nothing to do with type size, which is why the h4 here is the same 14px as the paragraph under it.
Both rails are <nav> elements with names — "Manual sections" and "On this page" — so they are two distinguishable landmarks in the list rather than two unnamed regions, and either can be skipped.

aria-current="page" belongs to the section nav and aria-current="location" to the on-this-page rail. Every entry in the rail is the page the reader is already on, so marking one of them as the current page contradicts the nav on the other side of the article.

The scroll-spy writes aria-current as the string "location" or the string "false" and the graphite rule is bound to the same expression, so the mark a sighted reader sees and the one a screen reader hears cannot disagree.

Every step and every h2 is a fragment target and none of them carries scroll-mt. The page relies on the system's one base rule, [id] { scroll-margin-top: 88px }, so a target added later is covered without anybody remembering to add a class to it.

A step's anchor is a real link with a real name — aria-label="Link to step 4" — and it is visible at rest. An anchor revealed on hover is unreachable from a touch screen and from a keyboard, which are the two ways this content is actually read.

A callout is a bordered block with its own text; the icon inside it is decorative and unlabelled, so the sentence has to state the severity itself. "Do not release the hold until the lab result is on the record" says what the amber triangle says.

The superseded notice is text in the reading order, above the lead and inside the article, rather than a colour or a banner over the page. It is the first thing said about the document, and it must be the first thing read.

The figure is a <figure> with a <figcaption>, and the caption is numbered so the sentence that refers to it has something to refer to. A screenshot standing in for an instruction needs the instruction in the prose as well — an image is not a step.

The table in prose carries a caption saying what it lists, <th scope="col"> on every heading and <th scope="row"> where the first cell names the row. It has no hover state, because nothing in it is a target.
The search field is labelled, its result count goes to a status region, and the empty case names what was typed. A list that silently empties reads as a search that crashed.

Raising a capital indent

SOP-PUR-004 · Revision 3 · Effective 01 Apr 2026 · Owner: Materials, Silvassa

Procurement

  • Onboarding a vendor
  • Raising a capital indent
  • Approval limits
  • Amending an order
  • Closing an order short

Quality

  • Inward inspection
  • QC hold and release

All 204 pages

A capital indent commits money that is not in the plant's operating budget, so it takes a budget code before it takes a vendor. This page covers indents raised at Silvassa and Vapi. For revenue purchases — consumables, spares, packing material — see SOP-PUR-002, Raising a purchase indent.

On this page

  • When an indent is capital
  • Raising it
  • Who approves it
  • After approval

When an indent is capital

An indent is capital when what is bought is expected to last more than one financial year and is carried on the fixed asset register. The test is the asset register and not the value: a ₹40,000 die that is capitalised is a capital indent, and ₹6,00,000 of packing film is not.

Three things make an indent capital regardless of what it costs:

  • Plant and machinery, including a rebuild that extends the life of an existing machine.
  • Moulds, dies and tooling held against a part number rather than consumed in a run.
  • Anything installed in the building — a compressor line, a weighbridge, a fire panel.

If none of the three applies and the item is still expected to last three years, ask Accounts before raising anything. Getting this wrong is expensive to unwind: the indent has to be cancelled and raised again under the other series, and the budget consumed in between shows against the wrong head until the month is closed.

Raising it

Open Materials → Indents → New and choose Capital as the type. The type cannot be changed after the indent is saved, which is the one field on the form worth reading twice.

A capital indent without a budget code will not route to anybody.

It saves as a draft and sits there. Nothing tells you, because nothing has been submitted.

The budget code is on the capital budget sheet the plant head circulates in April. It is eight characters — plant, year, head, serial — and it is written SIL-27-PM-04 on the sheet and typed without the hyphens.

What to attach

Two quotations for anything above ₹2,00,000, and three above ₹10,00,000. A single-source purchase needs a note saying why, signed by the plant head, attached to the indent and not sent separately.

Who approves it

The indent routes on its value, and the value is the whole indent rather than the line. Splitting one purchase across two indents to stay under a limit is the thing internal audit looks for first.

Approval limits for a capital indent, by value
Indent value Approver Also needs
Up to ₹2,00,000 Plant head —
₹2,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 Plant head, then Finance Two quotations
Above ₹10,00,000 Director Three quotations, board note

Limits are set once a year and are the same at both plants. They are listed again, with the delegation in force while an approver is away, in SOP-PUR-006, Approval limits.

After approval

An approved capital indent becomes a purchase order raised by the buyer holding that category. The indent stays open until the order is closed, so a partially received machine keeps its indent open and the budget stays committed against it.

At Vapi the budget code is allotted by Accounts, not by the plant head.

Everything else on this page is the same at both plants.

Last reviewed 12 Jun 2026 by Anil Kulkarni · Next review 01 Apr 2027

variants.name: Every element the body is made of
variants.html:
QC hold and release

SOP-QA-011 · Revision 5 · Effective 01 Jul 2026

A hold stops material moving. It is not a rejection and it is not a note on the record — while a lot is on hold nobody may issue it, and the store cannot override that from the issue screen.

What a hold does

Placing a hold writes a block against the lot in the batch ledger. The lot keeps its quantity and its location, so it is still counted in stock and still valued, and every issue against it fails with the hold reference rather than with a generic error.

A hold is placed by Quality and by nobody else. A buyer who believes material is wrong raises a re-inspection request against the lot, which is what puts it in front of Quality.

Three kinds of hold

The kind is chosen when the hold is placed and decides who may release it:

Inward hold
Placed automatically on every lot received against a material with an inspection plan. Released by the inspector who passes the lot.
Quality hold
Placed by an inspector on a lot already in stock, usually after a complaint from the line. Released by the QA head.
Customer hold
Placed against finished goods when a customer has raised a claim. Released by the QA head with the claim reference on the record.

Releasing a hold

A release needs a result on the record. Not a phone call, not an email to the store — the lab result or the inspection has to be entered against the lot first, because the release records which result it was made on and that link is what an audit follows.

  1. Open the lot in Quality → Holds.
  2. Check that the result you are releasing against is listed under the hold.
  3. Choose Release and enter the reason.
  4. The block clears on the next issue attempt, which is immediate.

A hold that has to stay while part of the lot is used is not a partial release. Split the lot first — Quality → Holds → Split — and release the child lot. Releasing and re-holding leaves a gap in the ledger during which the whole lot was issuable.

Who may release each kind of hold, and what the release needs
Hold Released by Needs
Inward Inspector Inspection result
Quality QA head Lab result
Customer QA head Claim reference

If the material has already moved

Material issued before a hold was placed is traced through the batch ledger and recalled by the QA head. That is a different procedure and it is SOP-QA-014, Recall of issued material.

Material that does not conform to specified requirements shall be identified and controlled to prevent its unintended use or delivery.

IATF 16949:2016, clause 8.7.1 — the requirement this procedure exists to meet.

The caption is numbered because the sentence above refers to it by number. A caption that only describes the picture cannot be referred to from anywhere else in the document, and a printed copy has no other way of pointing at it.

Booking a goods receipt

SOP-STO-002 · Revision 7 · Effective 01 Jul 2026 · Owner: Stores, Silvassa

Nine steps, about fifteen minutes for a single-vehicle receipt. Do them at the gate, in this order, before the vehicle is released — a GRN booked after the lorry has gone cannot be corrected against the weighbridge.

Before you start

  • The vehicle is on the weighbridge and the gross weight is recorded.
  • You have the vendor challan and, for a taxable supply, the e-way bill number.
  • The purchase order is approved and not closed.
  1. 1

    Check the challan against the order

    The challan carries the order number. If it does not, or it carries one that is closed, the vehicle does not come off the weighbridge until the buyer confirms which order it is against.

  2. 2

    Open the order in Receipts

    Stores → Receipts → Against an order. The screen scans a barcode as well, which is faster at the gate and is the same form either way.

    Open the receipt screen

  3. 3

    Enter the vehicle and the challan

    Vehicle number, challan number, challan date and the e-way bill. The e-way bill is required above ₹50,000 of taxable value and the form will not post without it.

  4. 4

    Weigh in and record the tare

    The net is gross less tare and the system computes it. Do not type a net weight over it: the two figures are what the vendor is paid on and a typed net that does not reconcile is found at the monthly weighbridge audit, by which time the vehicle is four weeks gone.

    A difference over 0.5% against the challan needs a shortage note before the GRN posts.

    Step 7 covers it. Do not adjust the weights to make the difference go away.

  5. 5

    Enter the received quantity per line

    Count what is on the vehicle, not what the challan says. The two columns sit beside each other on the screen for that reason.

  6. 6

    Post the GRN

    The number is allotted on posting — GRN-4821 — and it cannot be reused. A GRN posted in error is reversed and a new one raised; there is no delete.

  7. 7

    Raise a shortage note if there is a difference

    Short, excess or damaged, on the GRN itself, while the vehicle is still on site. The driver signs the shortage note and the copy travels back with the vehicle.

  8. 8

    Put the material away against the bin

    Material against an inspection plan goes to the quarantine bay and stays on inward hold until Quality passes it. See SOP-QA-011, QC hold and release.

  9. 9

    Release the vehicle

    Gate out against the GRN number. The gate register and the GRN reconcile nightly and a vehicle released without one is the exception the security supervisor is asked about the next morning.

Last reviewed 04 Jul 2026 by Sunita Rane · Next review 01 Jul 2027

variants.html:
Closing an order short

SOP-PUR-009 · Revision 2 · Effective 01 Apr 2026

An order is closed short when the balance quantity will never be received — the vendor cannot supply it, the requirement has gone, or the material has been bought elsewhere.

Before you close it

Closing short releases the committed value back to the budget and stops the order appearing in the pending-receipt register. It does not cancel anything already received and it does not touch an invoice that has been booked.

A short close is reversible for seven days.

After that the order is archived and reopening it is a request to Materials.

Tell the vendor before you close, not after. The order is what they are producing against, and a closure they hear about from the accounts department two weeks later is a claim.

Do not close an order short to make the pending register look clean at month end.

The commitment is what the plant is planning cash against. A closed order that is still coming is a payment nobody has provided for.

Where the balance is genuinely still expected but late, the answer is a revised delivery date on the order, which keeps the commitment and moves it out of the overdue count.

Who may close

The buyer who raised the order, up to a released value of ₹1,00,000. Above that it is the plant head, on the same screen, and the released figure is shown before the confirmation.

At Vapi a short close above ₹50,000 also needs the Finance controller.

Silvassa has no second approval on a short close. Everything else on this page is the same at both plants.

Both routes record who closed it and why, and the reason is printed on the order's own document. It is read by the vendor, so write it as something a vendor can read.

Amending an order

SOP-PUR-007 · Revision 4 · Effective 01 Apr 2026

Nothing in the manual matches “”.

  • Onboarding a vendor

  • Rejections and debit notes

An order is amended when a term on it changes after it has been approved — the quantity, the rate, the delivery date or the freight. Every amendment raises the revision number and reissues the document to the vendor.

What may be amended

Anything except the vendor and the plant. Changing either of those is a new order, because the first one has already been sent to a vendor who may have started against it.

  • Quantity, up or down, on a line that has not been fully received.
  • Rate, which re-routes the order for approval if the new value crosses a limit.
  • Delivery date, which is the amendment that does not need re-approval.

Raising a capital indent

SOP-PUR-004 · Revision 3 · Effective 01 Apr 2026

A capital indent commits money that is not in the plant's operating budget, so it takes a budget code before it takes a vendor.

On this page
  • When an indent is capital
  • Raising it
  • Who approves it

When an indent is capital

An indent is capital when what is bought is expected to last more than one financial year and is carried on the fixed asset register. The test is the asset register and not the value.

  • Plant and machinery, including a rebuild that extends the life of a machine.
  • Moulds, dies and tooling held against a part number.
  • Anything installed in the building.

Raising it

Open Materials → Indents → New and choose Capital. The type cannot be changed after the indent is saved.

A capital indent without a budget code will not route to anybody.

It saves as a draft and sits there.

Who approves it

The indent routes on its value, and the value is the whole indent rather than the line.

Approval limits for a capital indent, by value

To ₹10,00,000 Plant head, Finance 2 quotes

2 sheets · A4 portrait · SOP-STO-002 Revision 7 · a printed copy is uncontrolled from the moment it leaves this screen

K

Konspec Industries Pvt Ltd

Silvassa works · Standard operating procedure

Booking a goods receipt

SOP-STO-002 · Revision 7

Effective 01 Jul 2026

Document control

Owner
Stores, Silvassa
Approved by
Anil Kulkarni, Plant Head
Next review
01 Jul 2027
Supersedes
Revision 6, 01 Apr 2025
Applies at
Silvassa and Vapi
Printed
21 Aug 2026

Purpose and scope

Booking a receipt of purchased material at the gate, against an approved purchase order, at either plant. It does not cover receipts against a subcontracting challan, which is SOP-STO-005.

Procedure

  1. 1

    Check the challan against the order

    The challan carries the order number. If it does not, or it carries one that is closed, the vehicle does not come off the weighbridge until the buyer confirms the order.

  2. 2

    Open the order in Receipts

    Stores → Receipts → Against an order, or scan the order barcode on the challan.

  3. 3

    Enter the vehicle and the challan

    Vehicle number, challan number and date, and the e-way bill where the taxable value is above ₹50,000.

  4. 4

    Weigh in and record the tare

    The net is gross less tare and is computed. Do not type a net weight over it.

    A difference over 0.5% against the challan needs a shortage note before the GRN posts. Do not adjust the weights to make the difference go away.

  5. 5

    Enter the received quantity per line

    Count what is on the vehicle, not what the challan says.

  6. 6

    Post the GRN

    The number is allotted on posting and cannot be reused. A GRN posted in error is reversed, not deleted.

Referenced documents

  • SOP-QA-011, QC hold and release — material against an inspection plan.
  • SOP-STO-004, Short and excess receipts — differences against the challan.
  • SOP-STO-005, Receipts against a subcontracting challan.

Sunita Rane · Stores in-charge
